topic: Mintlify Agent Analytics Guide 2026: Measure AI Traffic to Developer Docs

competitors.title: Mintlify Analytics Documentation - Filter by AI or Human Visitors
key_points: Mintlify analytics dashboard shows page views, visitor trends, search queries, and content effectiveness
AI vs human traffic source filter separates agent traffic from browser traffic
For AI traffic: shows visitors, top agents, and MCP searches metrics
For human traffic: shows visitors, page views, assistant usage, searches, and feedback
Top Agents replaces referrals when viewing AI traffic — shows which AI platforms access docs
MCP Searches tab tracks how AI agents query docs via Model Context Protocol
Assistant tab shows categories (LLM-automated conversation grouping) and chat history
All analytics tabs exportable to CSV respecting current traffic source and time range filters

competitors.title: Analytics for AI and Agent Traffic — Mintlify Blog (Feb 2026)
key_points: Mintlify now shows exactly how AI agents interact with your docs — which agents visit, which pages accessed most, what searches via MCP
AI agents act as the interface between users and software — they read docs to answer questions, generate code, decide which APIs to call
Data collected by analyzing incoming user agents and matching against known AI agent signatures
Agents depend on clear structure, explicit definitions, and machine-readable signals — llms.txt, skill.md, content negotiation, MCP
Combined with consistent structure and predictable navigation, agent analytics lets teams design the agent experience instead of guessing

competitors.title: The State of Agent Traffic in Documentation (March 2026)
key_points: 790M requests over 30 days across Mintlify-powered docs — 45.3% AI agents, 45.8% browsers, 8.9% other
Claude Code alone: 199.4M requests (25.2% of total, 55.8% of AI traffic) — more than Chrome on Windows (119.4M)
Cursor: 142.3M requests (18.0% of total, 39.8% of AI traffic)
Together Claude Code and Cursor = 95.6% of all identified AI agent traffic
Other agents detected: OpenCode, Trae (ByteDance), ChatGPT, Google NotebookLM, Manus
Important caveat: OpenAI Codex doesn't send identifiable user-agent headers, so actual AI traffic share likely higher than reported
Context retrieval is the new page view — docs quality and structure directly shapes agent performance

competitors.title: Almost Half Your Docs Traffic is AI — Mintlify Blog (Feb 2026)
key_points: Agents that fail produce no signals — no bounce rate alert, no support ticket — just a developer who gets a wrong answer
Agents look for structure maps first (llms.txt) before reading any paragraph — this changes the entire starting experience
Content negotiation lets docs serve the same knowledge differently: rich pages for browsers, clean Markdown for agents
Mintlify AI traffic analytics answers: which agents visit, what pages they read, where they stop
When agents can move through docs and bring correct answers back, it builds trust and reduces hallucinations

competitors.title: Docs as an Abstraction Layer for Coding Agents — Mintlify Blog (June 2026)
key_points: Controlled experiment with large engineering org: Mintlify-generated docs + MCP vs no-docs baseline
Results: 64% more precise answers, 39% better discoverability, ~50% fewer tokens consumed per task, 1.5x faster completion
Structured documentation encodes intent alongside implementation — code tells you what got built, docs tell you why
Token reduction changes economics: if spending $1M/year on AI coding tokens, 50% reduction = $500K back
READMEs alone are snapshots that decay — automated workflows (Mintlify Workflows) keep the intent layer up to date

competitors.title: Mintlify Pricing — Agent Analytics is Enterprise-Only
key_points: Starter ($0): Full platform, custom domain, web editor, assistant, writing agent, workflows, MCP server, 5,000 credits
Enterprise (Contact): Everything in Starter plus agent analytics, advanced insights, role-based permissions, SSO, performance SLA
Agent analytics is gated behind Enterprise tier — only available with contact-sales pricing
Overage pricing: $0.01 per credit beyond included quota
Starter includes basic analytics; agent-specific analytics requires Enterprise upgrade

angles: The invisible audience: Why most teams don't know half their docs traffic is AI agents and can't measure agent satisfaction — no bounce rates, no support tickets, just silent failures

Agent analytics as demand gen: Margaret-Volpi (Mintlify Marketing) argues docs are the highest-traffic, highest-intent surface in the funnel — agents are now a second layer of traffic most companies don't even track
The Claude Code effect: One coding agent (Claude Code) pulls more documentation traffic than Chrome on Windows — a single AI tool now rivals the world's most popular browser

From page views to context retrieval: The metric that matters is no longer 'how many humans visited' but 'how well did agents extract and act on our content' — a fundamental shift in how teams should measure docs effectiveness
MCP as the missing analytics signal: MCP searches provide the highest-intent data — what agents are looking for but can't find — directly surfacing documentation gaps that traditional analytics miss

The Enterprise gate: Agent analytics is locked behind Enterprise pricing — teams on the free Starter plan can't measure agent traffic, creating a knowledge gap between docs teams and the AI tools that consume their content
Top agents as competitive intelligence: Seeing which AI platforms access your docs reveals user preferences, integration opportunities, and which agent ecosystems to prioritize for optimization
The quiet failure mode: Agents that can't parse docs don't complain — they serve wrong answers or silently switch to competitors, making agent analytics the only way to detect this failure
outline: Introduction: The invisible half of your docs traffic — why 45% of requests now come from AI agents
What Are Agent Analytics? Tracking AI tool consumption of your documentation
Why Agent Analytics Matter Now: Claude Code alone pulls more than Chrome on Windows — the silent failure problem
Mintlify's Agent Analytics Feature: Traffic source filter, top agents, page views, MCP searches, assistant categories
How Agent Analytics Work: User-agent header analysis, AI agent signature matching, content negotiation signals
The Agent Score Framework: AFDocs-based scoring of documentation agent-readiness (1,155 sites evaluated)
What the Data Reveals: 790M monthly requests — Claude Code 55.8%, Cursor 39.8%, OpenCode, Trae, ChatGPT, and others
Beyond Page Views: MCP searches as the highest-intent signal — surfacing documentation gaps agents can't fill
Agent Analytics in Practice: Monitoring traffic trends, identifying popular pages for agents, tracking integration opportunities
Transitioning from Human-Centric to Dual-Audience Metrics: Page views for humans, context retrieval success for agents
The Enterprise Barrier: Agent analytics is Enterprise-only — what Starter plan teams are missing
Building Agent-Friendly Docs with Data: Using analytics insights to optimize llms.txt, skill.md, content negotiation, and MCP integration
The Structured Docs Experiment: 64% better precision, 50% fewer tokens — why well-structured docs + MCP outperform raw code for agents
Automating Doc Quality with Workflows: Keeping the intent layer up to date so agent analytics shows improvement over time
Case Studies: Perplexity, X, Replit, Cognition, Laravel, Lovable — how Mintlify customers use analytics to serve both audiences
Future of Documentation Analytics: As more agents launch and the ecosystem broadens, agent analytics becomes essential infrastructure
Conclusion: Agent analytics is not optional — it's the only way to measure documentation ROI in an AI-native world
